title: PortaRegulus risk register exchange document
description: One file holds the risk components of NIST SP 800-221r1 ipd for one enterprise: context, governance roles, strategy, appetite, assets, registers, drivers, risks, responses and the forecast log. Each risk entry is a valid NIST IR 8286 Rev. 1 risk register entry (allOf). The risk detail uses NIST IR 8286 Rev. 1 risk detail record property definitions. Amounts are in the document currency. Probabilities are fractions from 0 to 1. Section numbers in descriptions refer to SP 800-221r1 ipd.

schemaVersion.description: Sec. 7.7. A 1.0.0 document is also a valid 1.1.0 document, because 1.1.0 adds optional fields only. The app writes 1.1.0.

identifier.description: Stable local identifier. Unique per kind in one document.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code. One currency per document. NIST IR 8286 fields marked ($) hold amounts in this currency.

representative.description: Number written to the NIST numeric field when only the label is known.

timeframeMonths.description: Window for riskLikelihood. SP 800-221r1 lines 1010 to 1011 ask for one consistent timeframe.

reportableEventThreshold.description: Smallest single-event impact that counts as an event for forecasts and outcomes.

kind.description: Sec. 3.8. An opportunity register holds positive risks only.

distribution.description: lognormal takes a calibrated 90 percent interval (lower, upper). pert takes min, mode and max (standard PERT, lambda 4). constant takes one value.

estimate.description: Quantitative estimate. frequency is events per year that are NOT caused through the linked drivers. impactPerEvent is the loss (negative polarity) or gain (positive polarity) of one event.

rationale.description: SP 800-221r1 Sec. 2.4.3. No estimate without a reason.

secondaryImpacts.description: Sec. 3.3.2 cascading risks and Sec. 3.4.2 secondary loss events. Each secondary impact happens with its probability after each primary event.

triggerProbability.description: Probability that one driver event causes one event of this risk in the same year.

driver.description: A shared cause. One driver event can cause events in several risks in the same simulated year (common shock).

frequency.description: Driver events per year. For a control driver, one event is one failure of the control.

impacts.description: SP 800-221r1 Table 6 ERR impact split, plus safety (SP 800-221r1 line 344).

category.description: Controlled category for aggregation across any risk source. The cause domain, not the consequence.

sourceRef.description: SP 800-221r1 Sec. 5.2.1 traceability, for example System A risk 1 tagged A-1.

rollUp.description: SP 800-221r1 lines 1637 to 1641 three-point roll-up of the source values.

disparityLayout.description: Table 10 Resolve risk register disparities. one-row-per-response or one-row-all-responses.

responseCostRule.description: Since 1.1.0. SP 800-221r1 lines 1661 to 1664. total is the sum of the source costs. exposure-weighted-average weights each source cost by its exposure rating, and is the plain mean when every exposure rating is 0. Without this field the cost is the total.

riskDetail.description: The NIST IR 8286 Rev. 1 risk detail record fields that the register entry does not already hold. The export builds the full RDR from these fields plus the register fields (SPEC.md Sec. 7.4).

currentRiskAnalysis.description: Required by the NIST RDR schema but not defined there. Fig. 15 row Current risk analysis.

residualResponseAsImplemented.description: Fig. 15 row Residual risk response as implemented. Not in the NIST JSON schema.

planned.description: Expected values after the planned response (RDR likelihoodAfterControlsWillBe, impactAfterControls, expectedExposureRating). For quantitative risks the engine writes them at export.

measured.description: Values measured after the response is in place. Empty until then.

implementedResponseDescription.description: Response already in place (Fig. 11 Current Risk Response).

risk.description: One risk register entry. allOf the NIST IR 8286 Rev. 1 risk register schema, so every entry is a valid IR 8286 entry. riskLikelihood is P(at least one event in the register timeframe). riskImpact is the mean annual impact given at least one event. exposureRating is riskLikelihood times riskImpact, which equals the expected annual loss or gain.

polarity.description: SP 800-221r1 Sec. 2.4.6 and 3.8. negative is a threat. positive is an opportunity.

responseDecision.description: pending means no response is decided yet. The NIST fields then hold an explicit interim Accept with cost 0.

defaultedFields.description: JSON Pointers (relative to this risk) of fields that an importer filled because the source did not hold them.

objectiveIds.description: Sec. 2.4.4 and 4.1. Enterprise objectives this risk affects.

horizon.description: Sec. 3.3. Emerging and horizon risks trigger a review of appetite and tolerance.

linkedRisks.description: Sec. 3.3.2 cascades and combinations, Sec. 5.4.3 trade-off between a positive risk and its negative risks.

onlyWithResponse.description: Sec. 3.6 lines 1072 to 1074. This risk exists only if the named response is funded. It is new risk caused by a response.

previousAssessment.description: Sec. 4.3 Fig. 11 Last column and Table 7 Previous Period. impacts is since 1.1.0, for the reputation and mission profiles of the previous period.

priorityOverride.description: Sec. 5.3.1, 5.3.3 and 5.4.4. A priority set by leadership, with the reason.

acceptance.description: Sec. 5.1.1 and 5.1.2. Record that the risk, or an exception to a tolerance, is accepted.

responseEffect.description: The estimate of one target after the response is in place. Only the given parts change.

responseOption.description: A candidate risk response that competes for budget.

reserveAmount.description: Sec. 3.6 and 3.7.1 risk reserve. Set aside in year 1 and released if the target risk does not occur.

bundleOf.description: Ids of options that this option combines. The effects of a bundle replace the effects of its parts.

informativeReferences.description: Sec. 3.6. For example a CSF 2.0 subcategory or an SP 800-53 control id.

introducesRisks.description: Sec. 3.6 lines 1072 to 1074. Risks with onlyWithResponse set to this option.

forced.description: Sec. 5.3.2 operational optimization and mandatory requirements. require funds first, exclude never funds.

trigger.description: The state in which a tolerance is breached or an indicator fires.

appetiteStatement.description: One column of SP 800-221r1 Table 9. Appetite, tolerances, controls, KPIs and KRIs.

toleranceCurve.description: Maximum acceptable annual probability that total loss exceeds each amount. Loss ascending, probability strictly descending.

history.description: Sec. 5.4.2. Earlier tolerance curves with the reason for each change.

forecast.description: A frozen prediction and its later outcome, for the Brier score.

context.description: Sec. 1.1 and 3.1. Mission, objectives, internal and external context, mission-critical functions.

kind.description: Sec. 2.3 and 4.1. The four enterprise objectives of the ERP.

functions.description: Sec. 5.1.1. Mission- and business-critical functions. Assets inherit their criticality.

disciplines.description: Sec. 1.1. ICT risk disciplines in scope, for example cybersecurity, privacy, supply chain, OT, IoT, AI.

governance.description: Sec. 3.1.1 and Table 1. Who holds which risk role at which level.

strategy.description: Sec. 3.2.2. Common scales, reporting cycle, budget ceilings, thresholds and the optimization method.

scales.description: Sec. 2.4.2. One scale set for every register in the document.

budget.description: Sec. 3.2.2 ceilings for CapEx and OpEx. The funding rule uses firstYearCash.

inclusionThreshold.description: Sec. 3.5. Risks with exposure below this amount need not stay in the register.

escalationThreshold.description: Sec. 5.2.2 and 5.3.3. Risks with exposure at or above this amount must appear in the parent register.

asset.description: Sec. 3.3.1. Mission-supporting asset with valuation. External assets are allowed.
